title: Where will you meet
your spouse?
summary: The clue your chart holds about where a life partner comes from: the keeper of your seventh house, in all twelve places it can be.
film: Where will you meet your spouse?
imageAlt: Maya in a house of twelve rooms, with the seventh room lit
basis: This guide uses your rising sign and the planets in your birth chart, which depend on your exact time of birth.
inside: The house of marriage and its keeper, explained simply
All twelve places the keeper can sit, and what each suggests
Your marriage planet by rising sign, and what else is read
intro: Astrologers are asked where and when someone will meet their partner more than almost anything else. For the where, the tradition has a simple and rather charming method. It looks at the house of marriage, finds the planet that keeps it, and sees which room of the chart that planet lives in.

This guide gives you the whole method. It is a clue, not a promise: one pointer among several that a full reading weighs together. But it is a good clue, and many couples recognise their own story in it.

sections.label: The method
title: Room seven
and its keeper.
paragraphs: A chart is divided into twelve houses, like a house with twelve rooms. The seventh is the house of marriage and committed partnership. It sits directly opposite the first house, which is you, because a partner is the person you face.

Every house has a keeper: the planet that rules the sign on it. The keeper of the seventh house is called the seventh lord. Wherever it sits in your chart, it carries the matter of marriage into that part of your life, and that is the part where a partner is most likely to appear.

sections.label: The twelve places
title: Where the keeper
lives.
paragraphs: Find the house your seventh lord sits in, then read across. The middle column is the short version.

rows.note: They come into your life through your own initiative: something you start, or simply by showing up as yourself.
Through family connections, a family gathering, or work around food, money or valuables.
Through a sibling, a neighbour, a short trip, a class, or by writing and messaging first.
Someone from your home town or close to your family, often a match your family knows of.
Through dating, college, a creative pursuit, a hobby, sport or entertainment.
At work in a day-to-day sense: a colleague, a client, or someone you meet through your routine.
Through social life, business dealings or a formal introduction. Read as one of the strongest placements.
During a time of big change, or through research, shared finances or a partner’s family circle.
On a journey, in higher study, or through a teacher, a place of worship or a mentor.
Through your profession: someone in your field, at a work event, or a senior you respect.
Someone from your circle or a friend of a friend, at a party, in a group or online community.
In another city or country, or a partner from a different land or culture; sometimes at a retreat.

after: Each line describes a setting, not a script. A seventh lord in the tenth house can mean a colleague, but it can also mean someone you meet because of your work: at a conference, through a client, or on a business trip.

sections.label: Your keeper
title: Your marriage planet,
by rising sign.
paragraphs: Which planet is your seventh lord depends on your rising sign, not on your Sun or Moon sign. The planet’s own nature also colours the partner: Venus is read as charming and artistic, Mars as energetic and direct, Jupiter as wise and generous, Saturn as mature and serious, Mercury as youthful and talkative, the Moon as caring, the Sun as confident and proud.

items.name: Planets in the seventh house
items.text: Any planet actually sitting in your house of marriage adds its own flavour to the partner and to how you meet.

items.name: Venus and Jupiter
items.text: Venus stands for love and partnership in every chart. In the tradition Jupiter is also read as the husband in a woman’s chart, and Venus as the wife in a man’s.

items.name: The navamsha
items.text: A second chart, drawn from the first by dividing each sign into nine parts, is read specifically for marriage. An astrologer always checks the clue against it.

items.name: The timing
items.text: When is read from your planetary periods. The period or sub-period of the seventh lord, of Venus, or of a planet sitting in the seventh house is treated as a window for meeting or marrying.

sections.label: Using it
title: What to do
with a clue.
paragraphs: Treat it as a hint about where to spend your time, not as a place to wait. If your seventh lord points to friends, say yes to more invitations. If it points to study or travel, enrol or go. If it points to work, stop keeping your working life and your personal life in separate boxes.
And if your own story does not match, that is normal. The rest of the chart can outweigh a single pointer, which is why a reading looks at all of it.

faq.q: How do I find my seventh lord?
faq.a: From your birth chart. You need your rising sign, which depends on your time of birth, and then the house where its seventh lord sits. Draw your chart on the home page and you can ask the astrologer directly.

faq.q: Can a chart tell me exactly who I will marry?
faq.a: No. It can describe the kind of person, the likely setting and the windows of time. It cannot name anyone, and anyone who claims to is promising more than the method can give.

faq.q: I’m already married and we met somewhere else. Is my chart wrong?
faq.a: Not necessarily. This is one pointer among several, and planets in the seventh house or the navamsha chart often tell the stronger story. It is still fun to check.

note: House meanings and rulerships are those of the classical Parashari tradition, with whole-sign houses.
